subject: AI & Agents
title: The Problem with Predictive Policing
description: One-minute skill: The Problem with Predictive Policing.

hook.text: An AI tells police to patrol a neighborhood more. Arrests go up. The AI says 'see, I was right.'

buildup.text: Predictive policing uses historical crime data to forecast where crimes will occur.

discovery.text: But historical data reflects where police looked hardest, not where crime actually happens most.

twist.text: More patrols in an area find more crime. This feeds back into the model, creating a vicious cycle.

climax.text: Los Angeles and other cities abandoned predictive policing after studies exposed the feedback loop.

punchline.text: The algorithm didn't predict crime. It perpetuated policing patterns.

quiz.question: What is the main problem with predictive policing?
options: It creates feedback loops from biased historical data
It is too expensive to implement
Criminals learn to avoid predicted areas

details.summary: Predictive policing uses AI to forecast where crimes will occur. Critics argue these systems recycle historical bias, directing more officers to minority neighborhoods and creating self-fulfilling prophecies.
details.whyItMatters: Predictive policing can entrench discriminatory patterns under a veneer of objectivity. Understanding its flaws is crucial for communities affected by over-policing.
takeaways: AI predicts crime hotspots using historical arrest data
Biased data leads to over-policing of minority neighborhoods
Feedback loops create self-fulfilling prophecies of crime

faq.question: How does predictive policing create self-fulfilling prophecies?
faq.answer: More police in an area means more arrests, which generates more data pointing to that area. The algorithm then sends even more police there, regardless of actual crime rates elsewhere.

faq.question: Are any cities moving away from predictive policing?
faq.answer: Yes. Los Angeles, New Orleans, and several other cities have abandoned their predictive policing programs after audits revealed racial bias and lack of proven effectiveness.
